decisions.reason: An adjustable cardboard quarter-pallet shelf display builds directly on the firm's core corrugated design and production know-how, so it can read market feedback and refine the product in-house.
A pegboard-back cardboard shelf display is a modest extension of existing display competence and lets the firm offer hanging-product solutions using knowledge it already holds.
The standard cardboard quarter-pallet shelf display is a staple of the firm's display portfolio and sits squarely within its established knowledge base and production capacity.
The eighth-pallet cardboard display uses the same design and manufacturing knowledge as the quarter-pallet versions and serves retailers' demand for compact placements.

A wooden display pallet lies further from the firm's paper-based expertise, which limits its ability to interpret results and improve the product, but it complements the one-stop offering, so it is kept under closer review.
The media-product quarter-pallet display rests on core cardboard competence, but the shrinking physical media market raises some risk, so it is kept while results are monitored.
